rationale: This is a TanStack Router type-mapping interface in the generated routeTree.gen.ts file. It maps route IDs to route types for type safety. As generated boilerplate it is not an element itself; the routes it references would be modelled as navigation routes.

Sidebar main navigation menu component rendering router links with active-state highlighting. It is a reusable, non-routable UI fragment composed into the app layout, so it maps to a UX library subview. It has moderate significance as the primary nav menu and implements user interface rendering only.

ItemsPublic is a SQLModel (non-table) response DTO that wraps a list of ItemPublic with a count. It is returned by the read_items route. As a schema describing a paginated collection shape, it belongs in the data-model layer as an object schema. It is a notable but minor element.

A shadcn/ui-style wrapper around the Radix Select trigger that renders a styled UI primitive. It belongs in the UX layer as part of a reusable component library, but it is a small subpart of the Select component, so its architectural significance is minor.

This is an inline arrow function in TanStack Router's generated route tree (routeTree.gen.ts). It only returns the parent LayoutRoute. The generated file is evidence for navigation routes, but this getter is generated boilerplate, not an element itself.

A POST HTTP endpoint in the login router, so it is modelled as an API operation. It looks up the user, generates a password-reset token and returns the rendered recovery email HTML. It is part of the credential-recovery surface, but it is an auxiliary preview endpoint, not a core boundary.

A React props interface for the EditUser dialog component. It is a trivial type declaration supporting the component and carries no behaviour of its own. It would be captured as attributes of the ux component rather than as a standalone architectural element.

Inline react-query mutation callback inside the DeleteUser component that only invalidates cached queries after the mutation settles. It is a trivial implementation detail of the component, not an architectural element in its own right.

An auto-generated (@hey-api/openapi-ts) internal options type for path parameter serialization in the generated API client. It is generated boilerplate and an implementation detail with no callers, so it is not an architectural element.

This is the HTTP route handler for POST /password-recovery/{email}, a credential-recovery API operation. It orchestrates the user lookup, reset-token generation and email dispatch, and returns a uniform response that prevents email enumeration. It is part of the authentication surface. Persistence and email sending are delegated to callees.

HTTP POST /users/ route on the private router (FastAPI template, typically local-only). It is an API operation that creates a user and persists it through the DB session. The password hashing is delegated, so it does not implement authentication itself. As a dev-only private endpoint, its significance is moderate.

Generated API client internal type (params.gen.ts) grouping body, headers, path and query parameters for request building. It is generated boilerplate scaffolding with no callers, below the granularity a maintainer would name as an architectural element.

Small React hook module that wraps the sonner toast library to show standardized success and error notifications. It is a UI feedback utility, best modelled as a reusable feedback pattern, but it is thin and of minor architectural significance.

Thin shadcn/ui wrapper around the Radix Tooltip Provider that only sets a default delay. It is generated-style UI boilerplate, not an architectural element. Its parent tooltip library component would be modelled instead. It does take part in rendering the UI context.

Playwright E2E test configuration that defines the browser project (Desktop Chrome), base URL, CI retries, reporters and the dev-server launch. It is test environment configuration, best modelled as a testing context variation (e2e/browser context). It is notable for the test setup but is not core architecture.

This core security module defines the application's authentication mechanism: JWT access-token issuance with HS256 and the secret key, plus Argon2/Bcrypt password hashing and verification. It is the authentication configuration evidence for the backend, an architecturally significant security element.

A trivial shadcn/ui wrapper around the Radix Sheet Trigger primitive that only adds a data-slot attribute. It is generated-style library boilerplate, not an architecturally meaningful UI component on its own, though it does render user-facing UI.

React dialog component rendering an admin edit-user form, triggered from a dropdown menu item. It is non-routable and composed into the admin view, so it is a reusable sub-view. It submits through the generated API client, so the call itself happens elsewhere. A notable UI unit within the admin area.

ItemUpdate is a SQLModel DTO schema (non-table) defining the update payload for items, with optional title and description fields and their validation constraints. It is a logical data shape, so it fits the data-model layer as an object schema of moderate significance.

HTTP route handler for POST /login/test-token, part of the API surface. It validates the access token through the CurrentUser dependency and returns the authenticated user, so it serves as an authentication check endpoint. It is not test code. The handler itself is trivial, so its significance is moderate.

Alembic migration downgrade step that reverts the UUID primary-key change on the user and item tables, restoring integer ids, sequences and constraints. It belongs to the data-store layer as part of a migration. The migration itself would be the modelled unit, not this function, so no element type fits and significance is low.

React dialog form component for editing an item. It renders a non-routable UI fragment embedded in item views and calls ItemsService.updateItem through the API client. As a UI module it belongs in ux as a subview; it is a notable but not core unit.

This is a generated (types.gen.ts) configuration interface for an HTTP client, holding only baseURL and throwOnError options. It is generated boilerplate with no callers or behaviour, below the granularity an architecture model would record.

Generated SDK client method wrapping the PATCH /api/v1/users/me operation. It is evidence for an API operation, but it is generated boilerplate in a client stub, so its significance is low. It performs an HTTP call to the backend. It only declares a bearer scheme and does no authentication work itself.

UserUpdate is a SQLModel (non-table) DTO schema that defines the optional properties accepted by the API when a user is updated, with validation constraints on its fields. It is a logical data schema, so it maps to a data-model objectschema. It is a notable but non-core variant of the User entity.

This is the frontend SPA entry point. It bootstraps the React app, configures the API client's base URL and bearer-token auth from localStorage, and handles 401/403 by clearing the token and redirecting to login. It also wires the router, query client and theme provider, so it is the application-level UX configuration.

A props type declaration for the Logo UI component. It is a typing detail of that component, not an element in its own right. Any props would be attributes of the ux component itself, so this interface is not modelled separately.

HTTP GET route handler for fetching an item by ID. It is an API operation contract. It reads the item from the database session and enforces an ownership/superuser permission check, returning 403 otherwise. Authentication is handled by the CurrentUser dependency, not by this route.

HTTP GET /health-check/ route is an API operation exposed by the backend, used for liveness probing. It is trivial in logic, returning True, but it forms part of the API surface a maintainer would name for operations and deployment checks. It touches no storage, auth, or telemetry itself.

Auto-generated @hey-api/openapi-ts core type definitions (HttpMethod, Client, Config, utility types) for the generated HTTP client. This is generated boilerplate scaffolding, not an architectural element. The API contract itself would be modelled from the OpenAPI spec, not these generic client typings.

A shadcn/ui-style styling wrapper around a Radix dropdown sub-content primitive. It is generated-style boilerplate within a UI kit file and has no callers. It sits below the granularity of a modelled UX element; the parent dropdown-menu library component would be modelled instead. It does render UI.

Generic boilerplate React hook module (shadcn-style) that detects a mobile viewport via matchMedia. It is a trivial UI utility with no callers recorded and no architectural identity, so it sits below the granularity of a modelled element. It does not render anything itself.

An inline arrow function in a table column definition that renders a screen-reader-only 'Actions' header label. It is a trivial rendering fragment of a column config, below the granularity at which a maintainer would name an architecture element, though it does render UI.

Generated SDK client method (sdk.gen.ts) that wraps a POST to /api/v1/private/users/. It is generated boilerplate. The API operation itself would be modelled from the backend route, not from this client stub, so it is not a standalone element. It does perform an outbound HTTP call.

A shadcn-style UI library module of reusable table primitives (Table, TableHeader, TableRow and so on) that are thin styled wrappers over HTML table elements. It is a reusable library component in the UX layer, but it is largely generated boilerplate, so its significance is low.

The root route component in TanStack Router's __root.tsx is the top-level layout that renders an Outlet for child routes, plus head content and devtools. As the root of the routing tree, it is best modelled as the navigation root route. It renders UI but contains no logic of its own.

This frontend authentication hook implements login, signup and logout. It stores the access token in localStorage and calls the backend login and user APIs. It also drives navigation and error toasts. It is the client's central authentication mechanism, so it fits security/authenticationconfig.

A props type for a UI password input component. It only extends the native input props with an optional error string. It is a boilerplate type definition below modelling granularity, so the component itself, not its props interface, would be the UX element.

A reusable React Email UI module exporting Callout and Detail presentational components with inline styles for email templates. It is a small library component in a shared email UI package, user-facing rendering only, with minor architectural weight.

A shadcn/ui form primitive module wrapping react-hook-form and Radix components. It is a reusable UI library component, but it is largely vendored or generated boilerplate. It has low architectural significance, though it does render user-facing form elements.

Generated OpenAPI client stub method that wraps an HTTP DELETE to /api/v1/users/me. It is generated boilerplate, and the endpoint contract itself belongs to the API operation, so it is not an element on its own. It does perform an outbound HTTP call to the backend, so external_integration is true. It only attaches a bearer scheme reference rather than verifying identity.

React UI component rendering the sidebar user dropdown menu, with a settings link and a logout action. It is a UX component composed from library primitives inside AppSidebar. Logout is delegated to the useAuth hook, so the component does not implement authentication itself. Notable but minor in the UI hierarchy.

Central application configuration module that loads environment settings from a .env file (database URL, secrets, SMTP, Sentry). It is best modelled as a configuration artifact in the technology layer. It defines settings and validates default secrets, but does not itself authenticate, persist data, or call external systems.

This is the HTTP POST operation for password recovery, an API surface element. It begins credential recovery by generating a reset token, which is authentication work. It also guards against email enumeration. Email sending and the user lookup are delegated to other helpers, so persistence and integration are not done here.

SQLModel base class (not a table) that defines the shared Item properties title and description, with length validation. It is a logical schema shared by the Item entity and its DTOs, so it fits data-model objectschema. As a base schema it is notable but not central.

Inline mutation success callback inside the ChangePassword component that shows a toast and resets the form. It is a trivial UI handler and an implementation detail of the component, not an architectural element. It does drive user-facing feedback, so the user_interface concern applies.

A shadcn-style reusable UI primitive wrapping the HTML input element with styling. It is a library component reused across login, signup and other views. It is a generic scaffolded primitive with low architectural weight, but it does render user-facing UI.

SQLModel schema (not a table) defining the user registration payload, with email, password length and full_name constraints. It is a logical data shape used as the registration API request body, so it is best modelled as a data-model object schema of moderate significance.

Auto-generated @hey-api/openapi-ts client core utility that maps function arguments into body/headers/path/query slots. This is generated boilerplate below the granularity of an architecture element. The generated API client as a whole might be modelled, but this params helper module is not.

A generated (auth.gen.ts) type in the OpenAPI client core. It describes how auth credentials are attached to requests, mirroring a security scheme shape. It is generated boilerplate scaffolding, not a modelled architectural element. It is a pure type that performs no authentication itself.

An HTTP PUT route on /items/{id} is an API operation contract, which places it in the api layer. It enforces ownership and superuser permission checks, so authorization is true. It reads and commits the Item through the database session, so data_persistence is true. Authentication comes from an injected dependency, not this symbol, so it is false.

A small presentational sub-part of a shadcn-style pagination UI library component. It renders an ellipsis indicator and has no callers or logic. It is a reusable UI component, but only a minor piece of the pagination library, so its significance is low.

A trivial props type declaration for the Sidebar Main component, holding only an items array. It is a component-local typing detail below modelling granularity. The component itself would be the UX element, not its props interface.

Small React UI component rendering an item ID with a copy-to-clipboard button inside the Items table columns. It is a user-facing interactive element that triggers a copy action, but it is minor and local to the columns file, so its significance is low.

An HTTP GET route on the items collection is an API operation. It applies an ownership-based access check, with superusers seeing all items and other users only their own, and it queries the database directly for paginated items and a count. Authentication comes from the injected CurrentUser dependency, so the route itself does not authenticate.

HTTP PATCH /users/me route is an API operation for updating the authenticated user's profile. It relies on the CurrentUser dependency for identity rather than verifying credentials itself. It enforces email uniqueness and commits changes through the database session directly, so it persists data.

A small type in a generated API client utility file (utils.gen.ts) that holds the path parameters and URL used for URL serialization. It is generated boilerplate and an implementation detail, not an architectural element. It has no callers or callees and implements none of the cross-cutting concerns.

A props type declaring the columns and data inputs for the DataTable component. It is boilerplate typing for a UI component; the DataTable component itself would be the ux element. On its own it is a typing detail below the architectural granularity cut-off.

An Alembic migration that alters the column types of the user and item tables (varchar length limits), so it belongs to the data-store layer. There is no dedicated migration element type; it is evidence for field elements rather than a field itself, so element_type is null. It changes the durable database schema.

Auto-generated @hey-api/openapi-ts client core module providing body/query serialization helpers (FormData, JSON, URLSearchParams). This is generated boilerplate and a formatting utility below architectural granularity. It is not itself an API contract or a client element.

Generated TanStack Router type map (routeTree.gen.ts) that keys route paths to route types for type-safe navigation. It is generated boilerplate. The routes themselves would be navigation elements, but this interface is not a node on its own.

Inline auth callback in the API client config that supplies the bearer access token from localStorage for generated client requests. It is the frontend's token-provisioning mechanism for authentication, a small but notable piece of the auth configuration. Reading localStorage is a session-token lookup, not durable domain persistence.

This is a shadcn/ui sidebar library module: a reusable UI component family made up of the provider, context and sidebar parts. It renders the user interface and drives toggle and keyboard interaction. It is a notable reusable UI building block, but it is generated scaffolding rather than core app logic. Persisting open/closed state in a cookie is a minor UI preference, not durable storage.

Build-tooling configuration file for generating the frontend API client from openapi.json. It is a configuration artifact, not runtime application behaviour, so it fits technology.artifact. It has low significance, since it only governs code generation and exists as scaffolding for the generated client.

File-based TanStack route module whose main content is the SignUp page: a routable view rendering the registration form with zod validation. It also has a redirect guard for logged-in users, but the module is best modelled as a UX view. The auth work is delegated to useAuth, so the authentication concern is false.

HTTP POST /login/access-token is the OAuth2 password-flow token endpoint, a system boundary entry point. It verifies credentials and issues JWT access tokens, so it implements authentication. Its database lookups are delegated to crud, so the route itself does no persistence.

An inline header render function inside a table column definition, returning a screen-reader-only 'Actions' label. It is a trivial UI fragment with no callers and no architectural meaning on its own. The enclosing columns definition or table would be the modelled ux element, not this lambda.

This is a trivial route option that only sets the page title meta for the reset-password route. It is boilerplate configuration inside a route definition, not an architectural element on its own. The route itself would be modelled in navigation, not this head callback.

This module is a shadcn/ui-style reusable Input primitive that wraps the HTML input element with styling. It is a library UI component in the ux layer. It is generic, largely generated design-system scaffolding, so its architectural significance is low.

Private validation helper on the Settings config class. It rejects or warns about the default 'changethis' secret values. This is configuration hygiene below model granularity: it verifies no identity and enforces no permissions. Its only caller is the settings validator, so it does not warrant an element of its own.

A thin shadcn/ui wrapper around the Radix Dialog Description primitive that only applies styling classes. It is generated-style UI boilerplate below modelling granularity. It renders UI, but the Dialog library component as a whole would be the element, not this sub-part.

A shadcn/ui generated wrapper module around the sonner Toaster that applies theme-aware icons and styling. It is a reusable UI library component, but it is largely boilerplate scaffolding with low architectural significance. It renders the user-facing toast notifications.

A Pydantic request-body model defined inline in the private API routes module. It describes the input shape of the private user-creation endpoint, so it is best modelled as an inline API schema rather than a canonical data-model entity. It is minor and local to that route file.

Utility module bundling email rendering/sending via SMTP and password-reset JWT generation and verification. It is a cohesive application module with an external SMTP integration, token-based authentication work and logging. It is notable but not a core boundary.

UsersPublic is a SQLModel response schema with a list of UserPublic records and a count. It is returned by the read_users route as a paginated collection. As a non-table DTO defining a data shape, it fits a data-model object schema of moderate significance.

This is a small generic type in a generated API client file (.gen.ts) that describes the shape of a server-sent event frame. It is generated boilerplate with no callers and does not merit a node in the architecture model.

HTTP route handler for PATCH /me/password, an API operation. It verifies the current password credential and hashes the new one, which is an authentication concern. It also commits the updated user record to the database session, so it handles data persistence.

Vite build configuration file: a technology-layer build artifact that defines the frontend bundling pipeline, plugins (React, TanStack Router, Tailwind) and output into the backend. It is notable for deployment structure but is configuration, not runtime behaviour.

A shadcn/ui-style wrapper around Radix Tooltip primitives: a reusable UI library component. It is a thin styling wrapper, likely scaffolded, and has no callers in the graph, so it has low architectural significance. It renders UI, so the user_interface concern applies.

A props type for a UI loading button component. It is a TypeScript interface that only extends HTML button attributes with asChild and loading flags. This is component typing boilerplate, not an architectural element; the button component itself would be the modelled ux element.

HTTP GET /me route on the users API returns the currently authenticated user. It is a distinct API operation forming part of the public contract. Authentication is handled by the injected CurrentUser dependency, not by this handler, so no concern flags are set.

Generated OpenAPI client stub method (sdk.gen.ts) wrapping PATCH /api/v1/users/{user_id}. It is generated boilerplate; the operation it calls would be modelled as an api.operation from the backend contract, not this client method. It performs an HTTP call to the backend, which counts as external integration.

File-based route module that defines the routable User Settings page, composing the profile, password and delete-account tabs. It is a routable view, so ux.view fits best; the route itself could also be modelled in navigation. It reads the current user via useAuth but performs no auth checks itself, and its superuser branch has no effect.

Auto-generated barrel file from @hey-api/openapi-ts that only re-exports client types and helpers. It is generated boilerplate with no behaviour of its own. The generated API client as a whole might be modelled, but this index module is not an architectural element on its own.

This is the FastAPI route handler for PUT /items/{id}, so it is evidence for an API operation. It enforces an owner-or-superuser permission check inline, which is authorization. It reads the item, updates it and commits through the database session, which is persistence. Authentication comes from the injected CurrentUser dependency rather than this function.

A React 404 page component rendered as the router's not-found fallback. It is a complete user-facing screen with a link back home, so it is best modelled as a UX view. It is a notable but peripheral UI element.

FastAPI router module defining the /users API surface, with ten route operations. It is best modelled as the API path grouping for the users resource. It enforces superuser authorization, verifies passwords, writes to the database via the session, and sends emails.

FastAPI router module mounting the /private prefix with a POST /users/ endpoint. It is the API surface for a local/dev-only user creation route. The handler hashes the password by calling a security helper and persists the user through the session. Its significance is modest because it is a single private endpoint group.

This is a generated OpenAPI client stub (sdk.gen.ts) that wraps a POST to /api/v1/password-recovery/{email}. Generated boilerplate is not an architectural element on its own; the API operation itself would be modelled from the backend route. It calls an external HTTP backend, so external_integration applies.

A small reusable React Email UI component: it wraps BaseHeading as a styled h1 and is reused by three email templates. It is a library component in the UX layer, but it is a thin styling wrapper with minor architectural significance.

A shadcn/ui Badge primitive: a reusable, mostly generated styling component with variants. It belongs in the UX layer as a library component, but it is boilerplate-level with no callers, so its significance is low. It renders UI only.

This is a generated (.gen.ts) helper type for path parameter serialization in the API client core. It is trivial boilerplate that only adds a value field to an options interface. It is not an architectural element.

A shadcn-style UI library module that wraps the Radix Tabs primitives with styling. It is a reusable UI component definition, so it belongs in ux as a librarycomponent. As largely generated boilerplate it has low architectural significance.

Generated generic type in the auto-generated API client (types.gen.ts) that describes the request data shape (body, headers, path, query, url). It is generated boilerplate scaffolding, has no callers and no domain meaning, and sits below the granularity of an architecture element.

A shadcn-style UI primitive: a styled div layout wrapper for dialog footers. It is a reusable library component but trivial, likely generated scaffolding, and unused (no callers). It belongs in the UX layer as a minor library component of low significance.

Trivial inner wrapper inside the useCustomToast hook that delegates to toast.success with a fixed title. Widely called, but it is a UI feedback helper below modelling granularity; at most the hook itself could be a ux pattern. It drives a user-facing notification, so user_interface is true.

React Email template module rendering the password-reset email. It is a user-facing presentation artifact composed from shared UI components (Layout, Heading, LinkButton), so it is best modelled as a UX view. It renders content only and performs no credential verification itself. It is a notable template within the email package.

An HTTP POST route on /test-email/ is an API operation. It is a utility endpoint that sends a test email through an external SMTP integration via send_email. It is a notable but non-core part of the API surface. In the FastAPI template it is typically superuser-gated by a dependency, but this handler does not itself check auth.

A small React component that wraps the items table content in a Suspense boundary with a pending fallback. It is a non-routable UI fragment inside the Items view. It is minor, essentially a loading wrapper, but it does render user interface.

A small utility that reads an email template file bundled with the code and renders it with Jinja. Its only callers are the email-generation helpers. It is a formatting helper below the granularity of an architecture element. Reading a static template is not durable-storage persistence.

This is the FastAPI application entry point. It builds the app, initialises Sentry tracing, configures CORS, mounts the API router and serves the frontend. As the system boundary and main backend component, it rates as core. The Sentry setup counts as both observability and an external integration.

Logout function in the useAuth hook. It ends the session by removing the access token from localStorage and redirects to /login. As session-termination logic it is evidence for the frontend authentication configuration. It is a small but notable unit, called by the Sidebar and by the account-deletion flow.

A non-table SQLModel acting as a request DTO for self-service profile updates. It defines optional full_name and email fields with validation constraints, so it is a logical data schema, not persistence. As a notable request schema in the user domain it rates significance 2.

Thin bootstrap wrapper that opens a DB session and delegates to init_db for seeding initial data. It is scaffolding below the granularity of an architecture element; the real persistence work happens in init_db, so no concern is implemented here directly.

SQLModel class with table=True defines the persisted user table: primary key, hashed password and creation timestamp columns, plus a cascade-delete relationship to items. It is the physical storage definition for users, so it is modelled as a data-store collection. It holds credential data but performs no authentication logic itself.

A shadcn/Radix-style styled wrapper for a dropdown checkbox item, part of a generated UI primitive library. It is a reusable UI library component, but a thin styling wrapper with no callers and minor architectural significance. It renders UI, so only the user_interface concern applies.

Auto-generated @hey-api/openapi-ts client utility module (query serialization, auth param injection, URL building). Generated boilerplate below the architectural granularity; the generated API client as a whole might be modelled, but this utils file is not an element.

A shadcn/ui-style sidebar primitive that renders a styled button (or Slot) for group actions. It is a reusable UI action element, but it is generated library boilerplate with no callers, so its architectural significance is minor. It renders UI and implements no other cross-cutting concerns.

FastAPI router module defining the /items CRUD API surface (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE). It groups operations under the items path and is a significant API boundary. It performs ownership/superuser permission checks and reads and writes the database through the session directly.

This is a TanStack Router module-augmentation interface in the generated routeTree.gen.ts file. It only provides type mappings for routes; the routes themselves are modelled from the route files. Generated boilerplate is excluded by the granularity rule, even though its content describes the navigation graph.

This is a TypeScript type that TanStack Router generates in routeTree.gen.ts. It only enumerates route path literals for type safety. As generated boilerplate it is not an architectural element; the routes themselves would be modelled from the route files or route tree, not from this interface.

A skeleton loading placeholder for the users table. It is a non-routable UI fragment shown while data loads. It is a minor presentational unit composed into the admin users view, so it maps to a UX subview of low architectural significance.

A React confirm-delete dialog component, non-routable and composed into the items view's actions menu. It renders UI and triggers an API call through the generated client, but it does not implement the integration itself. It is a notable UI unit within the items feature.

This is a generated OpenAPI client stub method in sdk.gen.ts that wraps GET /api/v1/users/me. Generated code is not an element on its own; the API operation itself would be modelled from the backend route. It does make an HTTP call to the backend and attaches a bearer scheme, but it does no credential verification itself.

A shadcn-style reusable UI primitive that renders a pulsing placeholder div. It is a library component in the UI kit, but it is trivial and generic, with a single caller. It has minor architectural significance and implements only user-interface rendering.

HTTP PATCH /me/password route is an API operation on the public surface. It verifies the current password and hashes the new one (credential handling, so authentication), then commits the updated user to the database. It is a significant contract endpoint for credential management.

POST /signup is a public HTTP API operation for self-registration. It checks for an existing email and creates the user through the CRUD layer, which persists to the database. It is an identity-related system boundary, but it performs no credential verification itself, so authentication is not flagged.

Generated client method binding the GET /api/v1/users/ operation, with a bearer security requirement. It is evidence of the 'read users' API operation consumed by the admin route. It is generated code, so it ranks only moderately significant. It performs the HTTP call to the backend but does not itself verify identity.

A TanStack file-route module defining the /recover-password route, with a beforeLoad redirect when logged in, and a page component rendering the recovery form. It is a navigable destination in the router, so it is modelled as a navigation route. Identity checks are delegated to isLoggedIn; the module itself renders UI.

A non-table SQLModel schema defining the JSON payload returned by the login access-token route (access_token, token_type). It is a passive data shape, so it is modelled as an object schema in the data-model layer. It only carries a token and does not verify identity itself.

A reusable, styled link component for email templates that wraps the react-email Link with fixed styling. It is a UI library component, but a thin presentational wrapper that matters little beyond the email UI kit.

Generated OpenAPI client boilerplate (.gen.ts): a small options type for path parameter serialization (explode/style). It is an implementation detail of the generated HTTP client, not an architecturally meaningful element.

SQLModel class with table=True defines the physical 'item' table. It has a primary key, a timestamp, and an owner_id foreign key to user.id with cascade delete. That is persistence structure, so it maps to a data-store collection and is a core stored entity of the application.

A shadcn-style reusable UI primitive wrapping the Radix Avatar root with styling. It is a library UI component that renders user-facing interface, but it is a thin styled wrapper with low architectural significance. It is used only by the sidebar UserInfo component.

An HTTP PATCH route on the users router (/users/{user_id}) is an API operation contract. It updates a user record, and the handler reads and writes the database through the session and crud calls. Admin-only dependencies are likely declared on the decorator, but this source shows no auth logic.

A trivial local async wrapper inside the DeleteItem component that forwards to the generated ItemsService.deleteItem client. It is an implementation detail of the UI component, not an architectural element. The external call is performed by the callee, not by this wrapper.

A shadcn-style sidebar sub-primitive that wraps the Input component with styling classes. It is a reusable UI library component, but a trivial styled wrapper with no callers, so its architectural significance is minimal.

CardTitle is a shadcn-style UI primitive that renders a styled div as part of the Card library component. It is a reusable UI library subcomponent, but it is minor and largely boilerplate, so its significance is low. It renders UI and has no other concerns.

An HTTP DELETE route on the items API is an OpenAPI operation. The handler enforces an ownership or superuser permission check and deletes the item via the database session, so it covers authorization and persistence. Authentication is supplied by the injected CurrentUser dependency rather than done here.

POST / route on the items router is an HTTP API operation creating an item. It persists via session.add/commit. It depends on the CurrentUser dependency for identity but does not itself verify credentials or check permissions; ownership is assigned rather than enforced.

This FastAPI dependency module defines the OAuth2 bearer scheme and decodes JWTs to resolve the current user. It also enforces the superuser privilege check and provides DB session injection. It is the central authentication/authorization enforcement point for the API, so it belongs in the security layer as authentication configuration.

The CRUD module is the repository/DAO layer that reads and writes User and Item records through SQLModel sessions. That makes it data-store access-pattern code. It also implements credential authentication, verifying password hashes and resisting timing attacks. Architecturally it is a significant persistence unit for the backend.

Private Pydantic model validator on the Settings class that defaults EMAILS_FROM_NAME to PROJECT_NAME. It is trivial configuration boilerplate and an implementation detail, not an architectural element, and it implements none of the cross-cutting concerns.

Module defines the application's database engine connection (SQLModel/SQLAlchemy engine from DATABASE_URL) and seeds the initial superuser. It is the physical persistence entry point, best modelled as the data-store database element. It reads and writes durable storage.

A trivial props interface for the ItemActionsMenu component, with a single field holding an ItemPublic. It is component scaffolding that would be captured as attributes of the UX component itself, not as a standalone architectural element.

Cookiecutter post-generation hook that normalizes CRLF line endings to LF in generated shell scripts. It is template scaffolding boilerplate, not an architectural element. It does read and write files on disk.

This is a shadcn/ui-style generated primitive: a styled span wrapper for a dropdown menu shortcut label. It has no callers, no logic and no application-specific meaning. It is boilerplate below the granularity of a UX library component element, though it does render UI.

A shadcn/ui-style checkbox module that wraps the Radix primitive with styling. It is a reusable UI library component, so it belongs in ux as a librarycomponent. It is largely generated boilerplate with no callers, so its significance is minimal.

Generated TanStack Router type in routeTree.gen.ts that lists the root route's children for type checking. It is generated boilerplate and not itself a navigation element. The routes it references would be modelled separately as navigation routes.

This is a generated (.gen.ts) configuration type for the hey-api HTTP client core. It is scaffolding inside a generated API client, not an architectural element. It only declares an auth token option and performs no authentication itself, and it has no callers in the graph.

A non-table SQLModel schema for the password-reset request payload: a token plus a new password with length validation. It is a logical data shape (a DTO or request schema), so it fits data-model objectschema. It holds credential data but performs no authentication itself.

A React component that renders the items data table, or an empty-state message when there are no items. It is a non-routable UI fragment embedded in the Items view, so it fits SubView. Data fetching is delegated to a query-options helper. It is a notable internal UI unit, not core.

A shadcn-style reusable Button UI primitive with variant and size styling, exported for reuse across views. It is a reusable library component in the UX layer. It is largely generated or boilerplate scaffolding, so its significance is moderate. It renders user-facing UI.

TanStack file route module defining the /reset-password route with a beforeLoad guard (redirects if logged in or no token), search validation and the ResetPassword view. It is primarily a navigation route resolving to a password-reset form. It participates in the credential reset flow and renders the UI.

Initial Alembic migration creating the user and item tables, with their columns, a unique email index and a foreign key. It is direct evidence for the data-store layer, defining core persistence collections. Although generated, it establishes the physical schema. It writes the database schema, so data_persistence is true.

Auto-generated @hey-api/openapi-ts helper module that serializes path/query parameters per OpenAPI styles. It is generated boilerplate made of formatting utilities, below the granularity of an architectural element.

A trivial styled wrapper around the Radix Select separator primitive. It is generated shadcn/ui boilerplate that only adds class names. It is a sub-part of the Select library component rather than an architectural element on its own, though it does render UI.

Auto-generated @hey-api/openapi-ts Axios client runtime: generic HTTP request plumbing, not an application-specific element. Generated boilerplate falls under the 'none' layer. It performs HTTP calls to the backend, so it is marked as external integration.

React confirmation dialog embedded in the user settings view. It drives deletion of the user's own account via the generated API client and then logs out. It is a non-routable UI fragment, so subview fits. Persistence and auth work happen in the callees, not in this component.

Generated API client stub for the POST /api/v1/login/access-token OAuth2 token operation. It is evidence of an API operation consumed by the frontend and is used by the useAuth hook. It submits credentials to obtain a token over HTTP. Because it is generated code, its significance is moderate.

A props type declaration for the DeleteItem React component. It is component-local typing boilerplate and would at most be an attribute of the ux component element, not an architectural element in its own right.

Trivial shadcn/ui wrapper around a Radix DropdownMenu Portal primitive that only adds a data-slot attribute. It is generated-style UI boilerplate with no callers or logic, below the granularity of an architecture element, though it does render UI.

A generic frontend utility module holding error-message extraction and name-initials formatting helpers. These are trivial formatting and helper functions below the granularity of an architecture element. It performs no I/O, telemetry or rendering itself.

This is a generated OpenAPI client stub (sdk.gen.ts) that wraps POST /api/v1/login/test-token. Generated boilerplate is not an element; the operation itself would be modelled from the backend route. It makes an HTTP call to an external backend, but it does not perform token verification itself.

HTTP POST route /reset-password/ is an API operation at the system boundary. It verifies a password reset token (credential handling) and updates the user's password in the database via crud, so it touches authentication and persistence. It is a significant public contract in the auth flow.

Routable page component rendering the password recovery form; a UX view reached via the /recover-password route. It calls LoginService through a mutation but does not itself verify identity, so the only concern it implements is the user interface. It is a notable screen rather than a core architectural element.

HTTP DELETE /users/me route: a public API operation allowing the authenticated user to delete their own account. It enforces an authorization rule that blocks superusers from self-deletion, and it deletes the user record via the DB session. Authentication comes from the injected CurrentUser dependency, so it is not implemented here.

This is the HTTP route handler for POST /login/access-token, the OAuth2 password-flow token endpoint. That makes it an API operation and the system's authentication entry point. The handler itself verifies credentials through crud, checks the user is active and issues a JWT. Database access is delegated to crud, so persistence is not flagged.

Generated (.gen.ts) internal type for the API client's parameter-building helpers. It describes field configuration for request parameter slots. It is generated boilerplate below architectural granularity, so it is not a model element.

This is an inline React Query mutation callback inside the EditUser component. It only invalidates the cached "users" query. It is a trivial implementation detail of the component, not an architectural element in its own right.

A shadcn-style reusable UI primitive wrapping a Radix Checkbox with styling. It is a library component in the UX layer, but it is largely generated boilerplate with no callers, so its architectural significance is low. It renders a user-facing interface element.

A simple dataclass that holds the rendered HTML content and subject of an email, passed between the email-generation utilities. It is a passive code-level data carrier, not a domain entity schema, so it is an application DataObject of minor significance.

Auto-generated TypeScript type definitions produced by @hey-api/openapi-ts, mirroring the backend OpenAPI schemas. As generated boilerplate, the module is not modelled as an element itself. The canonical schemas belong to the API or data-model layers via the OpenAPI document. The module only declares types and does no work, so no concerns apply.

A trivial props interface holding a single user field for the UserActionsMenu React component. It is component-local typing boilerplate with no behaviour. At most it would be an attribute of the UX component it belongs to, not an architectural element in its own right.

A props type for the EditItem React component, holding an item and a success callback. It is boilerplate typing for component properties. It would be captured as an attribute of the EditItem UX component rather than modelled as its own element.

CRUD query function that reads the User table by email via SQLModel select. It is a repository-style data access routine with many callers (auth, registration, password recovery), so it is best modelled as a data-store access pattern of moderate significance.

A props type for the DeleteUser component, holding only an id and a success callback. It is a minor detail of that UI component rather than an element in its own right; the component itself would be modelled in the ux layer.

This is the FastAPI handler for PATCH /users/{user_id}, so it is an API operation. It reads the user through the session and checks email uniqueness before delegating the update to crud. The superuser check is probably a route dependency rather than code in this body, so authorization is false here.

This is a generated (types.gen.ts) options type belonging to the hey-api HTTP client runtime. It is scaffolding inside the generated client, not a domain contract or named architectural element. It describes request configuration but performs no behaviour itself, so it is excluded as generated boilerplate.

A trivial computed property on the Settings config class that reports whether SMTP host and sender address are both configured. It is an accessor-level helper with no behaviour of its own, so it falls below the granularity of a model element.

A generated SDK client method that binds the POST /api/v1/items/ operation, with a bearer security requirement and typed request and response. Generated API clients are evidence for API operations, so it maps to the create-item operation. It performs the HTTP call to the backend, which counts as external integration. Being generated code, its significance is moderate.

This is a TanStack Router type map in the generated routeTree.gen.ts file, mapping full paths to route types. The routes it lists are navigation elements in their own right, but this generated typing interface is boilerplate and not a modelled element.

React Email template module rendering the new-account welcome email with credentials and a dashboard link. It is a user-facing rendered artifact composed of UI library components, best modelled as a UX view (email template). It is a notable but not core element, and it only displays credentials rather than verifying them.

A SQLModel/Pydantic schema describing the payload for user creation, extending UserBase with a validated password field. It is a domain data shape definition, so it belongs in data-model as an object schema. It is widely used but carries no behaviour of its own.

A TanStack Router module-augmentation interface that registers the router type for TypeScript type inference. It is pure type-level boilerplate with no runtime behaviour, so it does not count as an architectural element. The router configuration itself would carry the navigation element.

Generated SDK client stub (sdk.gen.ts) wrapping a POST to /api/v1/reset-password/. As generated boilerplate it is not an element itself. The API operation it mirrors would be modelled instead. It does perform an outbound HTTP call to the backend, and its credential relevance lies in the server-side handler.

A shadcn-style UI library button that toggles the sidebar: an interactive action component. It is generic UI-kit scaffolding with low architectural significance, used only by the layout route. It renders UI and has no other cross-cutting concerns.

A shadcn-style wrapper around the Radix Avatar Image primitive. It is a reusable UI library component that only adds styling, and it is a minor part of the avatar component set. It renders UI and has no other concerns.

A pydantic BaseSettings class that holds the application's central configuration: API prefix, secret key, database DSN, SMTP, Sentry and superuser settings. Its only behaviour is self-validation (a driver rewrite and a default-secret guard), so it is a passive DataObject. It is architecturally significant because every component depends on it.

Generated OpenAPI client stub method (sdk.gen.ts) wrapping a DELETE /api/v1/items/{id} call. As generated code, it is not an architectural element in its own right; the operation it calls would be modelled in the API layer. It performs an HTTP call to the backend, which counts as external integration.

A tiny options type inside a generated API client path serializer (.gen.ts). It is generated boilerplate and an internal implementation detail of URL parameter serialization, not an architectural element in its own right.

A private Pydantic validator on the Settings class that rewrites a Postgres DSN scheme to use the psycopg driver. It is a string-normalization helper inside configuration and has no architectural standing of its own. It performs no storage I/O itself.

Auto-generated (@hey-api/openapi-ts) type definitions for the Axios HTTP client's config, request options and result shapes. This is generated boilerplate with no behaviour of its own and is not an architecturally meaningful element. The generated client as a whole might be modelled, but this types file is not.

A shadcn-style UI primitive wrapper around Radix Avatar Fallback that adds styling only. It is a reusable library component in the UI kit, but it is thin generated-style boilerplate with minor architectural significance. It renders UI, so user_interface is the only concern.

This is an inline cell renderer inside a table column definition. It wraps UserActionsMenu in a right-aligned div. It is a trivial UI rendering detail of the admin users table, below the granularity of an architectural element, though it does render user-facing UI.

A trivial React props interface declaring only a children prop for the AuthLayout component. It is a type-level implementation detail of the component, not an architectural element on its own. It performs no rendering and no authentication logic.

The file is generated by TanStack Router, but it is the app's complete route tree. It composes every route (login, signup, password recovery, and the layout children admin/items/settings) under a root. That makes it the best evidence for the navigation graph root container, rather than discardable boilerplate.

A reusable shadcn-style UI library component that renders a responsive sidebar (a mobile sheet or a collapsible desktop panel). It is a LibraryComponent in the ux layer, used by AppSidebar. It is a notable UI building block but generic vendored library code, so significance is moderate.

A trivial TypeScript props interface for a sidebar UserInfo component, with two optional string fields. It is component-local typing boilerplate, not an architectural element. The component itself, not its props type, would be modelled in the UX layer.

Standard Alembic env.py boilerplate generated by the alembic template. It configures the context for offline SQL emission and runs migrations. It is scaffolding rather than a named migration or schema element. Offline mode emits SQL script output and does not write to the database itself.

Module defining the admin users data table column configuration (headers, cell renderers, actions menu). It is UI table structure, so it maps to ux TableColumn definitions. It is a notable unit of the admin users view, but only moderately significant. It renders the UI and does not enforce roles; it only displays them.

A React Email template that composes Layout, Heading and Callout into a complete rendered test-email message. It is a user-facing presentation unit, closest to a UX view, though it is not routable. It is a notable but modest template within the email package.

This is a generated (types.gen.ts) configuration interface for the hey-api axios client. It is code-generation boilerplate describing client options, below the granularity of an architectural element. The generated API client as a whole might be modelled, but this config type is not.

FastAPI router module grouping the /utils endpoints: a superuser-gated test-email route and a health-check route. It is part of the API surface, but a minor utility group. Authorization is delegated to a dependency, and email sending is delegated to app.utils, so the module itself implements no cross-cutting concerns.

A React component that renders the full-screen 404 page, with a link back to the home route. It is a user-facing screen, typically used as the router's not-found view, so it is modelled as a UX view. It is notable but not central to the architecture.

A TanStack Router route option that returns static page-title meta for the dashboard route. It is trivial configuration boilerplate attached to the route, not an architectural element on its own. It only sets the document title shown to the user.

Auto-generated @hey-api/openapi-ts utility module that serializes query key values into JSON-friendly shapes. It is generated boilerplate made of formatting helpers with no architectural role of its own, so it should not be modelled as an element.

This is an HTTP POST route, /login/test-token, that exposes an API operation for validating an access token. It returns the authenticated user, which the CurrentUser dependency resolves. The operation itself is an authentication check on the API surface. It is a minor utility endpoint in the login API, so significance is moderate.

This is a shadcn-style wrapper around the Radix Sheet overlay primitive that only applies styling classes. It is a UI library sub-part used internally by SheetContent, so it counts as a minor UI library component of low architectural significance. It renders UI and has no other concerns.

A Pydantic model validator that enforces non-default values for SECRET_KEY, the database password and the superuser password. It is a security hardening control against default credentials, best modelled as a countermeasure. It validates configuration rather than performing authentication, and its significance is modest.
